title: What is on repeat, out of a statement you paste in
variant: The reader's own data, and the reason it is a page at all
prompt: I have no idea what subscriptions I am paying for. Can you make me something I can paste my statement into?
note: The other reason a tool exists: not that the arithmetic is hard, but that the data cannot leave. A bank statement is exactly the thing nobody should paste into a chat, and a single file that reads it in the reader's own browser and forgets it is the honest answer -- which is why the opening line says so rather than burying it in the fine print. The sample is chosen to teach two things about the method. STREAMLINE TV goes from £10.99 to £12.99, which broke the first version of the detector, because comparing every charge to the median throws out any subscription that went up; comparing each charge to the one before it keeps it and earns the 'was £10.99' badge. And MARKET STREET FOOD comes back every fortnight but swings forty per cent in price, so it lands in a second table the page prints anyway, headed as what it is: recognized and deliberately not counted. A tool that shows you its near-misses is one you can calibrate. The limit it cannot fix is stated plainly: a yearly bill inside three months is indistinguishable from a one-off, and the sample contains one.
